- Overestimate prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3% relative to model output.
- When sentiment history shows strong positive sentiment (e.g., >0.3), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast peaks by 5–10% if sentiment is high or recent.
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative spikes (e.g., -1.96, -0.51), model often fails to adjust downward quickly; apply a downward bias of 2–5% to forecast mid-to-late period.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after a sharp upward move in history; cap forecast at 1–2% below the immediate prior peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows a recent negative trend (e.g., 3 consecutive negative values), reduce forecast by 2–4% for the next 3–5 days to avoid “overcorrection” lag.
